title: Asian tech stocks jump as bargain buyers boost battered AI trade
html:
Investing.com-- Asian semiconductor and technology stocks rallied on Thursday as bargain buyers stepped in to support a sector that was battered by mounting doubts over the long-term viability of the artificial intelligence trade.

The TWII was the best performer in the region, rallying 2.4% on strong gains in local chipmaking and electronics names. TSMC lagged, falling slightly, while electronics giant Hon Hai Precision, also known as Foxconn, surged over 3%.

South Korea's KOSPI added 1.2%, recovering marginally from a near 11-month low hit earlier this week and a 6% slump in the prior session. Memory chip giants SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics rose 5% and 2.5%, respectively, and were the top boosts to the KOSPI.

Sentiment towards Korean markets was also aided by the Bank of Korea sharply hiking its economic growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027.

Japan's Nikkei 225 jumped 1.6% on gains in major chipmakers including Advantest, Kioxia, and Tokyo Electron, which rose between 3% and 11%.

Asian markets were encouraged by a late-session recovery in Wall Street on Wednesday, where bargain buying helped the Nasdaq Composite rebound from its weakest level in nearly eight months.

While Wall Street still ended lower for the day, Wall Street futures advanced in Asian trade.

Tech stocks slumped through October and November amid mounting concerns over the long-term viability of the AI trade, especially amid rising interest rates and growing U.S. regulatory scrutiny.

Markets were also still grappling with the overhang from a governance crisis at AI major Nvidia, whose CEO Jensen Huang was abruptly ousted and reinstated in the past two weeks.

Nvidia struggled to recover despite Huang's reinstatement earlier this week, leaving markets on edge over a sustained recovery in broader AI stocks.

Ratings agency S&P put Nvidia's credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade, citing weakness in the chipmaker's governance.
